Usage: gb COMMAND [OPTIONS]

Commands:
  rom info|verify|diff|patch    Inspect, compare, validate, and patch cartridges
  asm compile|decompile       Assemble source or inspect/export ROM bytes
  project init|import|resolve  Create, import, and resolve source projects
  build                       Build an editable project or source file
  run                         Execute a cartridge in the bundled emulator
  test                        Check a cartridge against assertions
  debug                       Run a deterministic debugger script
  mcp serve                   Expose local utilities to an AI agent over stdio
  capabilities                Discover machine-readable contracts
  schema                      Retrieve versioned JSON Schemas
  version                     Print the toolkit version

Use gb COMMAND --help for details.
Legacy flat init/import/inspect/verify/disassemble/patch aliases remain supported.

All utility commands accept --json. Numbers accept decimal or 0x hexadecimal.
Writes refuse existing outputs unless --overwrite is supported and supplied.
Exit codes: 0 success, 1 operation failed, 2 usage error, 3 validation/assertion failed.

rom diff:
rom diff BEFORE_ROM AFTER_ROM
Compare physical ROM bytes without writing. Reports total changed bytes and ranges.
Previews are bounded to 64 ranges and 32 bytes per range, including for large ROMs.

All utility commands accept --json. Numbers accept decimal or 0x hexadecimal.

rom patch ROM PATCHES.json --output NEW_ROM [--overwrite] [--fix-checksums] [--allow-unguarded]
Patch file: [{"offset":336,"bytes":[0],"expected":[243]}]. Offsets are ROM file offsets.
Expected bytes guard against another ROM revision. Source files are never replaced.

Assemble with RGBDS and emit .gb, .sym, and .map artifacts.
Set RGBDS_BIN to the tool directory or put rgbasm and rgblink on PATH.

asm decompile:
asm decompile ROM [--offset N] [--count N] [--output FILE] [--overwrite]
Print a bounded candidate instruction listing (default offset 0x100, 64 instructions).
--output without range options writes full byte-exact RGBDS data source; a range writes a diagnostic listing.
Original symbols, high-level source, and code/data boundaries cannot be recovered.

run:
run ROM [--frames N] [--memory ADDRESS:LENGTH,...] [--assert FILE.json]
        [--buttons A,start] [--breakpoint ADDRESS] [--max-instructions N]
Run the bundled emulator with bounded ticks (default 60 frame budgets, max 3600).
Assertion file: {"memory":[{"address":49152,"bytes":[1]}],"registers":{"pc":336}}.
Breakpoint addresses are mapped CPU addresses, across all current ROM banks.
Exit 3 for failed assertions or an unreached requested breakpoint.

         [--buttons A,start] [--breakpoint ADDRESS] [--max-instructions N]
Run bounded execution and check required memory/register assertions.
Use gb schema assertions --json for the assertion file contract. Exit 3 on failure.

All utility commands accept --json. Numbers accept decimal or 0x hexadecimal.

debug:
debug ROM --script FILE.json
Execute step, frame, read, write, breakpoints, run, and assert operations in order.
Bus writes affect runtime RAM/IO/mapper state. Cartridge files are preserved.
Script: {"version":1,"commands":[{"op":"step","count":1},{"op":"read","address":49152,"length":16}]}
Use gb schema debug --json for the full contract.
